sentences.text: Schizorhiza possessed a robust snout featuring more than 1,800 denticles arranged in dense rows to create a continuous cutting edge on both sides.
The denticles on Schizorhiza's snout were replaced by smaller nested denticles within their roots while new rows grew from the tip of the snout.
The species Schizorhiza stromeri was first described by Wilhelm Weiler in 1930 based on rostral denticles found in the Nubian Sandstone of Egypt.
A second species, S. weileri, was named by Giselda Serra in 1933 based on rostral denticles discovered in Libya.
Schizorhiza belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Schizorhiza is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The species S. weileri is currently considered a junior synonym of S. stromeri.
Schizorhiza lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian periods.
Its fossils have been found in Africa, the Middle East, North America, and South America.
